newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends uneventful session higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends uneventful session higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended higher in dull dealings Tuesday, buoyed by commission house buying, trading sources said.
But producer selling capped gains and kept prices trapped in a narrow range, they added.

Most-active March ended 1.30 cents a lb higher, at 113.95, after ranging from 114.40 to 112.35. Spot December futures rose 2.70 cents a lb on the day, to 122.25, while the remaining months finished 1.00 to 1.20 firmer.
The closely watched December/March spread widened to 8.30 cents, up from 6.90 cents at Monday's close.
Traders noted the December contract went into its month-long notice period today in a surprisingly orderly fashion. As expected, no notices were issued Tuesday.
Open interest in December as of Monday stood at 2,387 lots, the equivalent of about 600,000 bags of coffee.

Meanwhile, the CSCE reported after Monday's close that U.S. certified coffee stocks fell by 150 60-kg bags in the week ended Nov. 15 to only 321 bags, the lowest level since the CSCE began tracking stocks in 1980.
The CSCE also reported there were 1,250 bags pending grading in Miami, the same number as last week.

The CSCE declined to specify why the coffee pending grading had not been certified, but said either the owner was still deciding whether to grade the coffee or samples had not yet shown up at the exchange.
The weekly CSCE drawdown comes on the heels of monthly consumer inventory data released last Friday, showing a sharp drawdown in U.S. warehouse coffee stocks.
U.S. supplies of green coffee fell by 351,000 60-kg bags in October, to 1,260,000 bags, the lowest level since the Green Coffee Association of New York began tracking inventories in January, 1988.

Although low stock levels should continue to be supportive for prices, one analyst said the market's run-up on tight near-term supplies could be limited as exports new-crop coffee from Latin America picked up.
"We do have Central Americans and Colombians coming in and putting a lid on prices," the analyst said. "But the low levels of stocks into the high consumption period should give underlying support."

Technically, traders pegged near-term March resistance at 115.00-115.50, with the next upside hurdle seen at 117.50. To the downside, support was put at the 112.00-cent level, with strong psychological support noted at at 110.00.
The day's volume reached an estimated 5,337 lots.
